messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] High error rate from tenant OrpheusCorp (private VPC). Multiple 502/504s via their dedicated NLB, spikes started ~08:44 UTC. Severity: customer-impacting. Paging oncall.
Ryan (oncall): acked. pulling up logs/console now. Is this hitting both ingress and egress or just egress path?
Maria P: I see healthcheck flapping on NLB TG: several targets OutOfService, 502s peaking. DNS for their custom hostname returns NXDOMAIN intermittently when we query from our healthcheck IPs.
Sam N (networking): interesting — NXDOMAIN + NLB 502 suggests either DNS propagation or a SG/NACL blocking health probes, or a route table change. Any recent deploys to that tenant's infra?
deploy-bot: deploy finished: orpheus-service v2.14.1 at 08:33 UTC (canary -> all). No rollbacks.
Alice (Customer Eng): Orpheus SRE says they saw increased 5xx starting 08:45 and users losing inbound API traffic. They haven't changed DNS on their side.
Tim (infra): I'm seeing a short-lived spike in NAT gateway connection resets from that VPC around 08:42-08:46. Could be conntrack saturation on egress proxies.
Ryan (oncall): ok, action plan: 1) validate DNS resolution from multiple vantage points, 2) check NLB target health + TG logs, 3) confirm no recent SG changes, 4) if needed, rollback ingress change or route traffic away. Maria can you run dig from healthcheck hosts and share results?
Maria P: dig +trace orpheus.example.com @8.8.8.8 -> sometimes returns NXDOMAIN, sometimes correct A. From internal healthcheck host: ```
;; QUESTION SECTION:
;orpheus.example.com.    IN A
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345
```
Maria P: From another node: ```
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, ANSWER: 1
orpheus.example.com. 60 IN A 10.12.34.56
```
Sam N (networking): That smells like split-horizon DNS or transient Route53 propagation between our resolver chain and customer TTLs. But healthcheck IPs resolving NXDOMAIN indicates maybe a caching resolver in path that got a stale negative cache after a recent record swap.
Tim (infra): checking security group change logs for the tenant's VPC at ~08:30-08:40: I see an automated guardrail adjustment that tightened egress SG rules for proxies (rule id sg-0a12b). It was applied at 08:31 by infra-ops-job.
Ryan (oncall): pinging infra-ops runbook owner @Sam?
Sam N (networking): I'm on it. If the egress SG blocked DNS (53/UDP) or health checks, that'll explain NXDOMAIN and NLB failing targets. Can infra ops roll that change back as emergency if confirmed?
Tim (infra): I can stage a rollback to previous SG (sg-prev-0f9) in 2 minutes. Need approval from oncall.
Alice (Customer Eng): Orpheus wants us to try a workaround before a rollback — they can temporarily point their origin to our dedicated pool if we can open a bypass path.
Ryan (oncall): Given customer impact, rollback approved. Tim please revert the guardrail change and confirm healthchecks. Also let's add a temporary L7 route to direct Orpheus traffic to a healthy dedicated pool as fallback.
Tim (infra): starting rollback now. Command:
```
aws ec2 modify-security-group-rules --group-id sg-0a12b --remove-rules '[{"IpProtocol":"udp","FromPort":53,"ToPort":53,"IpRanges":[{"CidrIp":"0.0.0.0/0"}]}]'
```
Tim (infra): rollback applied at 08:57 UTC. Confirming connectivity.
Maria P: re-running dig from healthcheck host -> NOERROR now consistently. NLB target group shows most targets transitioning back InService.
Sam N (networking): I also flushed internal DNS caches for the affected resolver cluster and triggered a TTL refresh. Monitoring edge resolvers for negative cache purge.
Alice (Customer Eng): Orpheus SRE reports upstream latency normalizing and fewer 5xx. They're continuing smoke tests.
Ryan (oncall): Good. Let's keep traffic on primary for 15m and monitor SLOs. If errors reappear, we'll cut traffic to dedicated pool and do a controlled rollback of the service deploy.
Maria P: keeping watch on metrics: 5xx rate dropped from 18% -> 0.7% in last 5m. Healthcheck failures dropped to single-digit.
deploy-bot: alert: orpheus-service v2.14.1 retention metric shows increased error budget usage during 08:40-08:50.
Sam N (networking): still seeing a handful of resolvers with stale NXDOMAIN cached; performing a targeted cache purge job for resolver-az-a.
Tim (infra): confirming no further egress conntrack saturation after rollback. NAT metrics stable.
Alice (Customer Eng): Orpheus says they're comfortable leaving production traffic; they want a post-incident call to understand the guardrail change that caused this.
Ryan (oncall): Agreed — postmortem requested. Immediate next steps: 1) collect SG audit trail, 2) capture resolver cache states, 3) record NLB TG flapping logs, 4) schedule 1h blameless review with Orpheus and infra-ops. Assigning owners: Tim (SG audit + rollback details), Sam (DNS cache traces + purge script), Maria (NLB TG logs + metrics snapshot), Alice (customer coordination + call scheduling).
Tim (infra): noted. I'll export audit logs and config diff and drop into the incident folder.
Sam N (networking): will produce a short script to detect negative-cache spikes and add an alert to prod-resolvers.
Maria P: saving snapshots: nlb-target-snap-1719461120.tar.gz uploaded to incident artifacts.
Alice (Customer Eng): scheduling meeting w/ Orpheus for 14:00 UTC. Sending calendar invite.
Ryan (oncall): I'll keep monitoring for another 30m and then move to post-incident state. Thanks all for rapid response. Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident status changed to MITIGATED by Ryan (oncall) at 09:07 UTC. Closed paging. Please follow the postmortem template within 48h.
Ryan (oncall): tagging for follow-up: infra-ops-policy review required to prevent automated guardrail tightening during active tenant rollouts. Add to sprint backlog.
Alice (Customer Eng): Orpheus appreciated quick turnaround. They requested clearer pre-notice for guardrail changes going forward.
Maria P: adding telemetry alert for NLB TG flapping + resolver NXDOMAIN correlation.
Sam N (networking): will open a doc with remediation playbook: 'private-vpc-dns-shadowing-and-sg-rollback'.
Ryan (oncall): closing thread in 1h if stable. Good job everyone!"
